decisions.question: Are the Versioning entry 'Amended within v1, at bus-api@v1's request (its Refinement 3) ... as topology-dsl@v1's read row already applies it' (line 426) and the Validation paragraph describing docs/auto-run/experiments/topic-model-multi-writer/ ('replays the surface and reject sets of topology-dsl@v1, topology-ir@v1 and bus-api@v1 ... bus-api@v1's pass only with the amendment', line 439) live citations or historical text?

options.label: Historical, keep v1
options.consequence: The amendment entry keeps naming the version that requested the amendment and the read row that already applied the rule at the time; the experiment description keeps naming the fixture sets it actually replayed. Five occurrences stay at v1 and the final gate's stale-version scan sees them.

options.label: Live, move to v2
options.consequence: The text would claim that bus-api@v2 requested an amendment made before v2 existed and that the multi-writer experiment replayed v2 fixture sets it never ran, which is false.

decisions.why: The orchestrator's H7/H8 rule names a dated amendment entry and an experiment's description of what a version did as historical. Line 426 is an amendment entry without a date, but it records a past event (bus-api@v1's Refinement 3 request) and the state of topology-dsl@v1 at that moment; line 439 describes what an experiment ran. Moving either would make it false. topology-dsl@v2's read row still applies Lineage.root() to a state topic's initial value (topology-dsl.md line 379), so nothing the entry implies became false under v2.

decisions.question: Three live citations of bus-api@v1 sit inside this contract's own normative text: two doc comments in the Interface's Dart declarations (Tracing: 'What the bus and its observers do with an untraced topic is bus-api@v1's'; StateTopic.computed: 'When the bus calls createInitial() is bus-api@v1's') and guarantee G27 ('A publish path typed over MultiWriterTopic<T>, as bus-api@v1's Bus.publish and Publisher.publish are, therefore does not compile for a state topic'). The touch may change no declaration or guarantee. Do these citations move?

options.label: Move the version only
options.consequence: The doc comments and G27 name bus-api@v2; no declaration, signature, default or promise changes, and G27's reject fixture and behavior case are untouched. Valid only if bus-api@v2 still states each cited fact.

options.label: Leave them at v1
options.consequence: The declarations and G27 stay byte-identical, but they keep citing a superseded version, which the intake's Done-when forbids and the final gate reports as stale.

decisions.why: The intake record lists guarantee citations as live, and a doc comment that says which contract owns a behavior states what holds now. Each cited fact holds in bus-api@v2 unchanged: G30 still gates observers on Tracing.disabled and still delivers an untraced topic's values to subscribers; G6 still says when createInitial() is called (once, when the subject is created, which v2 places at activate whether or not the activation is connected); Refinement 3 and the Interface still type Bus.publish and Publisher.publish over MultiWriterTopic<T>. So the move changes the citation, not what G27 or the declarations promise.
evidence: hsdd/contract/bus-api.md (Refinement 3, Interface lines 126 and 170, G6, G30, G40)

decisions.question: 'How the lineage functions are applied' ends 'bus-api@v1 applies publishedTo at every publish and Lineage.root or Lineage.causedBy at shell publishes'. bus-api's G12, identical in v1 and v2, makes every shell publish a root message (fresh correlation id, no causation, no parents), and both versions list 'a shell publish linked to the delivery that prompted it (causation from shell code, Guide §10.2)' as not in the version. The 'or Lineage.causedBy' is wider than bus-api states, but v2 did not make it so. Does the touch restate the sentence?

options.label: Move the citation, keep the wording, report it
options.consequence: The touch stays inside the orchestrator's rule (restate only a sentence the new version makes false). The disjunction remains true, since bus-api applies Lineage.root, but over-wide; a reader may infer bus-api sometimes applies causedBy at a shell publish. The finding goes to the orchestrator.

options.label: Restate as 'Lineage.root at shell publishes, which are root messages (its G12)'
options.consequence: The sentence becomes exact. It is a wording change this intake did not cause, made in a stable contract's own lineage paragraph under a touch whose remit is citations a new version changed.

decisions.chosen: Move the citation, keep the wording, report it
decisions.why: The orchestrator's touch rule (S64.orchestrator.json) restates a sentence only when the new version makes it false, and the intake reports, never silently rewords, citations whose meaning changed. This one did not change meaning between v1 and v2 (G12 and the Not-in list are the same text), and the disjunction is not false. The over-width dates from topic-model's authoring at S06, before bus-api existed. Close call: a rule that the touch should also tighten pre-existing over-wide restatements would have made me restate it, at no risk to any fixture.
evidence: hsdd/contract/bus-api.md G12 and Versioning 'Not in v2'

decisions.question: How does this touch classify against topic-model's Versioning (Breaking list, Compatible list), and what happens to version, status and phase_ids?

options.label: No interface change: stays v1, stable, phase_ids final, no Versioning entry
options.consequence: Only citation versions in prose, doc comments, one guarantee's illustrative clause and two fixture comment lines change. No declaration, default, rule, guarantee promise or fixture behavior changes, so neither list applies; consumers re-read nothing and replay the same fixtures. The registry projection is unchanged.

options.label: Compatible amendment within v1 with a Versioning entry
options.consequence: Records the touch in Versioning as an amendment, as the MultiWriterTopic change was. Adds a change-log line for something no consumer can observe, and the Versioning section would mix interface amendments with citation housekeeping.

decisions.chosen: No interface change: stays v1, stable, phase_ids final, no Versioning entry
decisions.why: The Breaking and Compatible lists classify changes to the interface; a citation version is neither. The intake record classes topic-model as 'Unchanged except citations' (Landings), and the orchestrator's H7 rule calls a restatement of another contract's rule a compatible wording change, of which this touch made none. Git history carries the touch. The signal that would change my mind: a project convention that every edit of a stable contract leaves a Versioning line, which neither hsdd-contract nor this tree has.
